data.title: Phuket Jewish New Year event cancelled on security grounds
data.description: A Jewish New Year celebration in Phuket was cancelled at the last minute on Friday evening because of concerns raised by Israeli security officials, organisers said.

data.title: Bangkok Blue Line train disrupted, passengers diverted
data.description: Passengers using the MRT Blue Line in Bangkok on Saturday afternoon were forced to alter their routes after a signalling system failure suspended services on a 12-station stretch for more than two hours before repairs were completed.

data.title: Bangchak says no leaks found in Bangkok fuel pipeline
data.description: Bangchak Group said no leaks were found in a fuel pipeline along Chuea Phloeng Road in Klong Toey district of Bangkok following an inspection after thousands of litres of oil-contaminated wastewater were reported in the area.

data.title: Pathum Thani bank robbery suspect arrested in Bangkok
data.description: PATHUM THANI - Police have arrested a man accused of robbing a bank at gunpoint in Khlong Luang district and later setting fire to the car used in the heist to destroy evidence.

data.title: Illegal weight-loss products worth B50 million seized
data.description: Unregistered weight-loss injection pens and related materials worth more than 50 million baht were seized on Friday at a house in Nonthaburi, where the seller had been earning an estimated 8 million baht a month from online sales for the past year.

data.title: Senate collusion witness says testimony was forced
data.description: A witness in the Senate collusion case sought to retract his testimony, claiming he had been coerced into implicating the Bhumjaithai Party, according to a leaked document obtained by reporters on Friday.

data.title: JIC boss says temple wasn't targeted
data.description: The director of the Thailand-Cambodia Joint Information Centre (JIC) has rejected Cambodia's allegation that Thailand attacked Preah Vihear Temple.

data.title: Neglected facilities draw public scrutiny
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA: Residents of this northeastern province are questioning the management of state-funded projects after a public library and observatory costing nearly 90 million baht were closed and left to deteriorate for more than a decade.

data.title: Witness says testimony was forced
data.description: A witness in the Senate collusion case sought to retract his testimony, claiming he had been coerced into implicating the Bhumjaithai Party, according to a leaked document obtained by reporters yesterday.

data.title: Jewish cemetery faces probe
data.description: The Interior Ministry has ordered an investigation into the company that owns a Jewish cemetery in Chachoengsao over potential links to nominee businesses and money laundering.

data.title: Capitalising on 'waterway belt'
data.description: Every month, hundreds of containers carrying tissue paper leave southern China for Thailand, making their way by sea to Laem Chabang before the products eventually reach convenience stores, restaurants and households across the country.

data.title: Senators turn on Nakharin
data.description: Pisit Apiwattanapong and some fellow senators have criticised former Constitutional Court president Nakharin Mektrairat for questioning the Senate's political legitimacy and attributing an allegedly false statement to chief charter drafter Meechai Ruchuphan.

data.title: A little family affair
data.description: The upcoming no-confidence debate could produce one of the more intriguing political spectacles in recent parliamentary politics: an uncle and his nephew standing, in effect, on the same side of the chamber against the government.

data.title: House vows OECD-ready parliament
data.description: House Speaker Sophon Zarum has pledged to make parliament a model of good governance as lawmakers and anti-graft campaigners join efforts to help Thailand secure membership of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) by 2028.

data.title: Thai HIV doctor wins WHO regional award
data.description: A Thai HIV specialist has become the first Thai recipient of the World Health Organization's South-East Asia Regional Award for Public Health Champions.

data.title: Thailand tries to woo global drugmakers
data.description: The Public Health Ministry is in talks with 10 global pharmaceutical companies to attract investment in Thailand, with MSD emerging as the first major partner, deputy government spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana said.

data.title: Training boosts logistics careers
data.description: Labour Minister Julapun Amornvivat praised public-private cooperation in developing skilled logistics workers after 147 companies hired graduates of a government-supported training programme.

data.title: PM orders airport link reprieve
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has ordered the State Railway of Thailand (SRT) to urgently resolve problems with the Airport Rail Link and ensure uninterrupted service.

data.title: 'Thai Travel Plus' scheme heads towards cabinet vote
data.description: The "Thai Travel Plus" stimulus scheme will be submitted to the cabinet for approval on Sept 22, Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Pancharoenworakul said, adding that it is expected to generate 20 billion baht in economic activity.

data.title: Korat’s B90-million white elephant
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA - The sad state of a library and observatory, built at a cost of 90 million baht but later closed and left to deteriorate for years, has residents of Nakhon Ratchasima questioning the management of government-funded projects.

data.title: Former abbot, woman remanded in temple embezzlement case
data.description: Police presented the former abbot of Wat Phutthaisawan in Ayutthaya and a woman accused of acting his accomplice to their first remand hearing after investigators alleged that more than 100 million baht in temple donations had been misappropriated.

data.title: Two DSI officials arrested in exam-fraud case
data.description: Duo linked to ‘Mayor Heng’ reportedly handled B55 million in payments from job aspirants

data.title: Korat’s almost B90M in abandoned public facilities raise questions over state spending
data.description: NAKHON RATCHASIMA — Locals of Nakhon Ratchasima have begun questioning the management of state-funded projects after a public library and observatory, built at a cost of nearly 90 million baht, had public access rescinded and were left to deterioriate for over a decade.
